title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: For sufficiently large $k$, if $k$ is even, then $m(P_k) = k!/2$ and if $k$ is odd, then $m(P_k) = \frac{k-1}{4}(k-1)!$.
context_text: $P_k$ is the path on $k$ vertices. The Ramsey number $r(H)$ is the least $n$ such that every two-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$, and the threshold Ramsey multiplicity $m(H)$ is the minimum number of monochromatic copies of $H$ over all two-colourings of the edges of $K_{r(H)}$. Gerencsér and Gyárfás showed $r(P_k)=k-1+\lfloor k/2\rfloor$. Harary and Prins, who determined $m$ for stars ($m(K_{1,k})=1$ for $k$ even and $2k$ for $k\ge3$ odd), asked for $m$ of paths and cycles. The authors prove $m(P_k)\ge(ck)^k$ and $m(C_k)\ge(ck)^k$ for an absolute constant $c>0$. The conjectured values come from the colouring $\chi(a,b)$ of $K_{a+b}$ on $A\cup B$ ($|A|=a$, $|B|=b$) in which $A$ and $B$ are blue cliques and all $A$–$B$ edges are red: with $a_0=k-1$ and $b_0=\lfloor k/2\rfloor-1$, $\chi(a_0,b_0)$ has no monochromatic $P_k$; for $k$ even, $\chi(a_0+1,b_0)$ and $\chi(a_0,b_0+1)$ on $r(P_k)$ vertices each have exactly $k!/2$ monochromatic $P_k$, and for $k$ odd, $\chi(a_0,b_0+1)$ has exactly $\frac{k-1}{4}(k-1)!$. These show the lower bound is tight up to $c$, and the authors conjecture they are optimal for large $k$. They make an analogous conjecture for cycles.

paper_title: Threshold Ramsey multiplicity for paths and even cycles

title: Conjecture 4
statement_text: For sufficiently large $k$, if $k$ is even, then $m(C_k) = \frac{k-3}{2}(k-2)!$ and if $k$ is odd, then $m(C_k) = (k-1)!/2$.
context_text: For even $k \geq 6$, a modification of the extremal coloring $\chi(a_0+1, b_0)$ obtained by recoloring one edge in the blue clique of order $k$ to red yields exactly $\frac{k-3}{2}(k-2)!$ monochromatic $C_k$; for odd $k$, the coloring $\chi(k, k-1)$ yields $(k-1)!/2$ monochromatic $C_k$. The authors conjecture these are optimal for large $k$.
